angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 820,230 km at 64.96 pc = 0.17 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 15.3934 +/- 0.0177 mas (same row, RUWE 0.93): 64.96 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.179 +/- 0.011 solar radii from Gandolfi et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1203.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025arXiv250910136G/abstract): 820,230 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.886 +/- 0.036 solar masses from Gandolfi et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1203.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025arXiv250910136G/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5737 +/- 62 K from Gandolfi et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1203.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025arXiv250910136G/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Gandolfi et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1203.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025arXiv250910136G/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1203.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.242, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
